name: HELYON for Helix Stadium
subtitle: Unofficial mobile editor
promotionalText: Edit your Helix Stadium presets from your phone or tablet. Arrange effects, adjust parameters, and manage snapshots over Wi-Fi or a compatible USB connection.
description:
Unofficial mobile editor for the Helix Stadium.

HELYON is a free, independent editor for Helix Stadium and Helix Stadium XL.

Build and adjust your signal chain from your phone or tablet. Add, replace, bypass, and reorder effects; edit amp and effect parameters; browse presets and setlists; name snapshots; and save changes to your device.

Connect over your local Wi-Fi network or a compatible USB connection. USB editing requires Stadium firmware 1.4 or later, a data cable, and a phone or tablet that supports the Stadium USB network connection. On iPhone and iPad, the system chooses the route to your device address.

Try the offline preview to explore block editing without hardware. The preview does not produce audio. Live editing requires a compatible Helix Stadium. Original Helix and HX devices are not supported.

An optional extended DSP budget lets you attempt edits beyond the normal estimated budget. It is off by default, requires confirmation, and resets when you disconnect. This does not increase the device’s processing power and may cause rejected edits, audio dropouts, or instability. Back up your presets and use a spare preset.

No account, advertising, or analytics. Preset editing happens directly between your device and HELYON.

HELYON is not affiliated with or endorsed by Line 6 or Yamaha. Helix, Helix Stadium, Line 6, and Yamaha are trademarks of their respective owners.
reviewNotes:
HELYON is an independent, unofficial controller for user-owned Helix Stadium / Stadium XL hardware. No login or Line 6 cloud account is required. Preset editing communicates directly with the device using local OSC over Wi-Fi or compatible USB networking, after the owner enables Remote Access. The app does not install firmware or bypass device authentication for preset editing.

Changes addressing guideline 5.2.1:
- All 24 extracted category and connection icons have been replaced with original artwork.
- Copied parameter-help text has been removed and replaced with original general explanations.
- Song upload has been removed, including the native SFTP module and editor-derived credentials. Showcase browsing, selection and playback remain local control features.

Model identifiers, parameter labels/ranges and factory Focus tone definitions remain for interoperability and the optional tone pads. HELYON is not affiliated with or endorsed by Line 6 or Yamaha. Product names identify compatible hardware and its controls. Please identify any specific remaining content, trademark use or feature requiring documentation, and clarify whether your authorisation request applies to local, owner-enabled preset control itself.

Review without hardware: tap Try offline preview on the connection screen. Add/remove and reorder blocks, adjust parameters, bypass effects, and try Focus View. The preview does not produce audio or simulate device saving, song playback, setlists or hardware DSP behaviour.

Live editing: enable Remote Access on the Stadium, use the same Wi-Fi network, and allow Local Network access. Select a discovered device or enter its name/IP address. Compatible USB networking requires Stadium firmware 1.4+ and a data cable. Wait for Saved to Stadium before switching presets.

DSP figures are catalogue estimates, not live CPU readings. Advanced settings includes Extended DSP budget, off by default with a warning confirmation. It raises the app estimate from 66 to 82 per path for that connection and resets on disconnect. It does not modify device firmware or remove device validation.

validation.localNativeBuilds: iOS simulator Release (ad-hoc signed) and Android Release passed

validation.androidUsbCrash: Original release crash reproduced on Android API 34. Patched release survived five repeated USB attempts with no wired network; guidance displayed and process stayed alive. Patch application verified against a fresh dependency package.
